top.title: Notre Dame volleyball to play Assumption in KHSAA state championship
top.description: Just as they have done all year, the Notre Dame Pandas volleyball team overcame a bit of adversity to take down Whitley County 26-24, 19-25, 25-14, 25-14 in the 2026 Kentucky High School Athletic Association state semifinals. "It's a hard match when you don't have any history with another team. We just knew that they were going to come out and give it everything that they've got. We just couldn't let up. We had to figure out a few things and make a few adjustments," Notre Dame co-coach Hannah Colvin said. Even though they played in the second semifinal of the day, the Pandas came out a little sluggish, allowing the Colonels to surge to a 16-13 lead in the first set. But five straight points, highlighted by two Teagan Kondik aces, gave them an 18-16 lead. Behind 13th Region Player of the Year Regan Isaac, Whitley County took a set point at 24-23 before kills from Ellie Breitling and Kondik gave the Pandas a 1-0 advantage. Isaac, Shelbi Carroll and Jada Smith continued to wreak havoc on the Pandas' defense in the second set, combining for 16 kills, Regan responsible for 12 on her own. Despite hitting .220, the Colonels benefitted from six Panda attack errors. "(Isaac) was really good. Our game plan was to keep it away from her and get in her head to make mistakes. That second set, we were making more mistakes than they were," Notre Dame senior Ellie Osterkamp said. In the third set, NDA played a deeper back row to take away Isaac's preferred corner attack angle. While that put more responsibility on the block, NDA came up with two rejections and forced Whitley County into seven more attack errors. The Pandas grabbed a 4-0 lead, then surged to a 11-5 advantage after five straight Colonel errors. Dara Jackson finished off the set with the first of her two aces. "Between the first two sets and the last two, we made that adjustment and really came up with the defense in the back. That's something that we always instill, but really going after single ball is the most important and not giving up the play," Notre Dame co-coach Madison Salkowski said. The trends continued into the final set as three Whitley County errors gave Notre Dame a 4-1 lead. Emma Redlinger, who finished with 12 kills, had three straight terminations for a 9-4 advantage. The kill shot was a 6-0 NDA run led by four kills from Kondik. Just as the Colonels confused the Pandas with their varied attacks, NDA had four reliable options throughout the match. Kondik led the way with 21 kills, Makayla Roose had 13 and Ellie Breitling put away nine attacks. "We realized after the first couple sets that they were really leaning in on Teagan, too. We were finding ways to split their block and make sure that we weren't just giving Teagan a double block every time," Colvin said. Now, nationally-ranked Assumption awaits in the final match of the season. top.title: Could Gina Hinojosa reshape Texas Tech's board and put Cody Campbell's chairmanship at risk?
top.description: Texas Tech regent Cody Campbell and Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark clash over a potential Friday night game, escalating tensions over scheduling and control. (LM Otero/Associated Press) Texas' blue wave could cost one of college sports' most powerful billionaires a seat on the Texas Tech University System Board of Regents and put his chairmanship at risk. Cody Campbell, a former Texas Tech offensive lineman and oilman, has wielded significant influence over the Red Raiders since Gov. Greg Abbott appointed him to the board in 2021. Campbell's six-year term expires Jan. 31, shortly after Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa takes office. The governor appoints regents, who must be confirmed by the state Senate. The Texas Tech board elects its chair from among its members, so Hinojosa's appointments could affect who leads it. The Senate remains under Republican control and could serve as a check on her choices. As chairman, Campbell has become an influential figure in Texas Tech athletics and the broader debate over the future of college sports. He also took a public role in the program's response to quarterback Brendan Sorsby's legal battle over his sports betting history. Campbell, co-founder and co-CEO of Double Eagle Energy Holdings, became a billionaire through the oil and gas industry. He is a close ally and adviser to President Donald Trump on college sports, serving on both Trump's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition and his college sports council. He was also among the earliest members of the America First Policy Institute, a conservative think tank associated with the Trump administration, and has been a major donor to Republican candidates. Even if Campbell loses his board seat, he could retain significant financial influence over Red Raiders athletics. He and business partner John Sellers founded the Red Raiders' NIL collective, which supports player recruitment and roster retention. top.title: 3 keys to victory for the Broncos against the Panthers
top.description: After the difficult schedule the Denver Broncos have faced through eight weeks of the 2026 season, the Carolina Panthers likely look like a welcome relief for most. However, in the NFL, there is rarely such a thing as an "easy win." The Panthers will have had nine days to prepare for a home game against the Broncos . They will also have the advantage that the East Coast team has when a team from the West Coast makes the long trip for an early kickoff. Head coach Sean Payton will have his team ready to keep its momentum rolling, looking for a fifth straight win, but the Broncos will need to follow these three keys to get that win and avoid a big letdown on the road. Broncos' keys to victory over Panthers in Week 9 Get after Bryce Young The Panthers are going to try to establish their rushing attack, led by Chuba Hubbard, to attempt to negate the Broncos' pass rush. The Panthers have allowed 23 sacks this season, the second-most in the league, and their offensive line is missing starting right tackle Taylor Moton, who is out for the season. The Broncos need to come after Bryce Young on every passing down in this game. As strong as the secondary is, Vance Joseph can trust it to hold up in this one and dial up frequent blitzes to have Young scrambling just to get the ball out of his hands on nearly every dropback. This is the kind of game where the Broncos not only could have a bunch of sacks; they should. Expose Carolina's run defense The Broncos have struggled to move the ball on the ground this season, averaging only 92.6 rushing yards per game, 26th in the league. But the Panthers rank 30th in defending the run, giving up almost 141 yards per game. This is the game for the Broncos to get that running game going. Jonah Coleman had a solid performance last week against the Kansas City Chiefs, and if he can follow that up with another big game here, the momentum from that could carry into the latter stages of the season. If the Broncos can establish the run in this game and rip off six- or seven-yard chunks at a time, it will open things up for the offense and make the third key to victory that much easier to accomplish. Be aggressive with Bo Nix While the Panthers have struggled to defend against the run, they have been much more difficult to throw against, ranking 10th in the league in that category. Still, the defense as a whole has not been good. The Panthers gave up 59 points to the Chicago Bears in a game this season and that was at home. Payton needs to be aggressive with his play-calling and allow Bo Nix to open things up in the passing game. Nix should attempt to throw the ball deep down the field in this one, especially if the Broncos can get the run game going and he can use the play-action to his advantage. No disrespect to Carolina as an opponent, but the Broncos should use this game to boost the level the offense is currently playing at and see if they can develop some trends to carry through the rest of the season. top.title: Wolff delivers verdict on costly Mercedes call that left Russell furious
top.description: Toto Wolff has defended Mercedes' decision to instruct George Russell to back off during his final qualifying attempt at the Brazilian Grand Prix , describing it as a 50-50 call despite admitting the Briton deserved pole position. Russell was left furious during the closing stages of Q3 at Interlagos after being told to abandon a promising lap when he encountered Alex Albon's Williams ahead of him. The Mercedes driver was already second behind Lando Norris and appeared capable of challenging for pole, having set purple times in the first two sectors. However, his race engineer instructed him to slow down, with the team expecting another opportunity before the rain intensified. That opportunity never came, prompting an angry reaction from Russell over team radio , with Wolff himself intervening to remind the driver that he was still second. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Wolff reveals how close Russell was to Norris Speaking to Sky Sports F1 after qualifying, Wolff acknowledged the difficulty of making the right decision as the weather deteriorated: "If we were to have a crystal ball to know whether you should back off or not, that would be helpful It was a difficult one, a 50-50 call. He was running into Albon." Wolff also revealed how close Russell was to Norris at the moment the instruction was given, although he questioned whether the Briton would ultimately have completed a lap fast enough to take pole. "He was 18 milliseconds up on Norris at that stage. I don't think it would have been enough for pole, but he drove perfectly all session and merited to be on pole." Despite his doubts about whether Russell could have beaten Norris' benchmark, Wolff praised the Mercedes driver's performance throughout the rain-affected session: "He deserved it but you can't make that call. It's 50 per cent right or wrong. George was in a league of his own today." Russell ultimately finished qualifying second, 0.204 seconds behind Norris, but will start Sunday's race from seventh following a five-place grid penalty for a power unit change. His teammate Kimi Antonelli, who qualified third, will instead line up alongside Norris on the front row.

top.title: Michael Carrick backs Bruno Fernandes and insists attitude is ‘as good as ever’
top.description: Michael Carrick said Bruno Fernandes ’ attitude is “as good as ever” and he has no doubts about his commitment again after their falling-out. The United manager dropped his captain after Fernandes criticised his tactics during the 4-1 defeat to Como and chose not to bring him on in the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth. But Carrick and Fernandes held talks last week and the Portuguese returned to the team at Chelsea on Saturday before playing his part in their comeback win over Roma, scoring their first goal with a twice-taken penalty and providing the assist for Matheus Cunha’s equaliser. “I think by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and frame of mind he was in for that, I think that tells everything,” said Carrick. “Yeah, Bruno's as good as ever.” The 45-year-old has not revealed if Fernandes apologised to him, adding: “What's actually said in that discussion, you'll be pleased to know I'll keep that to myself. “But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me of what he brings to this team and this club, and I think he showed that again this week.” Carrick has challenged Cunha to replicate his catalytic display against Roma, when he won a penalty and scored two goals, to double his tally for the season. “He has to repeat that performance,” the United manager said. “He was fantastic and that's close to his best, and that's the level where we want to see.” Carrick has said before that he has not sought reassurances about his position during United’s slump and they have only won one of their last 10 games in all competitions. He has not been told he will remain in charge next week. “No, no,” he replied, adding that his plans were unchanged. “Just carry on as absolute normal.”

top.title: Torreense boss sends Celtic warning ahead of crucial Europa League showdown
top.description: Torreense boss sends Celtic warning ahead of crucial Europa League showdown New Torreense manager Joao Nuno insists his side are determined to continue their remarkable Europa League campaign when they welcome Celtic to Portugal later this month. Europa League Draw. Photo UEFA.com Martin O’Neill’s side will travel to Leiria for their next European fixture, with the match taking place around 50 miles from Torreense’s home in Torres Vedras due to their 2,000-capacity stadium failing to meet UEFA requirements. The Portuguese second-tier outfit, who currently sit 12th domestically, recently appointed Nuno following the dismissal of Luis Tralhao, despite the latter guiding the club to a historic national cup triumph over Sporting Lisbon last season. Torreense have exceeded expectations in Europe, sitting 19th in the Europa League standings compared to Celtic’s 32nd position, with the Portuguese side firmly in contention for a play-off place. Nuno enjoyed a remarkable start to his tenure on Thursday night as his ten-man side secured a dramatic 3-2 victory over Ararat Armenia, scoring twice in stoppage time despite playing more than an hour with a numerical disadvantage. Speaking after the victory, Nuno said: “That was an unforgettable night for everyone at Torreense, for the people at the club. “Given how the season has gone, it was an important win for the fans. Everyone identified with what we are trying to do. “It was an absolutely epic victory and I could not ask for a better debut as a manager. “Celtic are next here, so we will fight to do everything to try to get points and try to win the game. “Let’s continue our dream because we have done beautiful things in Europe this season. “We want to continue fighting to dignify Portuguese football and I think today we lived up to its standards and the Portuguese people can be proud of us.” HAVE YOUR SAY – Join the Celtic conversation in our comments section below… Celtic in the Fifties by Matt Corr, in two volumes, both published on 4th September 2026 by Celtic Star Books. top.title: Josue De Paula Understands What’s Holding Him Back With Dodgers
top.description: Los Angeles Dodgers No. 1 prospect Josue De Paula dipped his feet into MLB towards the end of the 2026 season, and impressed just about everyone with his performances over an 11-game span in the regular season. He hit a home run and drove in seven runs, posting an OPS over 1.000 and an on-base percentage of .500. While his offensive abilities are irrefutable, just about everyone knows what the 21-year-old needs to improve if he wants to earn a spot as a starter in the Dodgers’ outfield: his defense. “I think with [De Paula], we’ve talked through it and he’s fully aware of continuing to improve defensively,” general manager Brandon Gomes said . “We’ve all seen what he’s capable of in the box which is incredibly exciting. With that being said, we have a very talented core group already here, so I think it’s finding those opportunities but also making sure that throughout this offseason and coming into spring training that he continues to improve and get to that bar and gets to be an above average defender. “We’re not looking just to be like, ‘Oh, De Paula got pretty good.’ I think his mindset, and our coaching staff and all of ours is to make him as good of a defensive outfielder as we can to be a full player because that’s what we expect of all of our guys that step on the field.” Oct 6, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Josue De Paula (95) warms up prior to a game against the Atlanta Braves in game three of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images How Has De Paula Responded to Criticisms of His Defense? De Paula understands this criticism better than anyone, and is determined to prove his doubters wrong. “We’re going to keep working at it and come back better,” said De Paula. “…I know that’s a big area of improvement for me. I know I get a lot of hate on it. I’m that type, if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. So I’m gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon.” De Paula only got one opportunity in the outfield during his stint in MLB last season, recording a putout in his only opportunity to make a play across six innings. He also featured for the Triple-A Oklahoma City Comets in the outfield during the Triple-A postseason, and had a perfect fielding percentage through three games. De Paula’s agent, Scott Boras, expects the young star to train with former Gold Glover Jackie Bradley Jr. in the offseason, as he looks to improve with the glove. If De Paula manages to take a step forward defensively , he will be a key player for the Dodgers during the upcoming season.

top.title: UConn football QB Kalieb Osborne faces growth opportunity after UNC loss
top.description: EAST HARTFORD — For weeks, every step forward seemed to come a little bit easier for UConn quarterback Kalieb Osborne . The first-year starter looked increasingly comfortable with running coach Jason Candle’s offense, gaining confidence with each drive. Then came Saturday’s rainy game against North Carolina and Bill Belichick — the architect behind the New England Patriots’ dynasty. For 60 minutes, UNC made Osborne feel uncomfortable in the pocket, forcing him into mistakes that he hadn’t shown before. Every lesson came at full speed, and the growing pains seemingly all took place in UConn’s 38-21 loss at home. Osborne’s stat line still contained signs of promise as he completed 17-of-35 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns. But it also told the story of a quarterback learning just how thin the margin of error can be at the highest level. He threw two interceptions, including a pick-six, and lost a fumble in a performance that helped swing the momentum toward the Tar Heels . “I didn't have my best game, and it's stuff that I gotta improve on,” Osborne said. Yet inside the locker room, there is little concern about what Saturday’s struggles might say about what Osborne has been and what he can be. Teammates and coaches instead point to the progress he's shown throughout the season. “I got 100% confidence that he will bounce back,” wide receiver Ryder Treadway said. “It’s not all on him. There are 10 other guys out there that are doing stuff and trying to win, but he's been awesome. He just keeps getting back up and keeps fighting.” Candle said he thinks that Saturday’s game was the next step in Osborne’s development, believing the quarterback who has shown he can get better with each game can use this experience as fuel for his next leap forward. #UConn coach Jason Candle on today’s loss to North Carolina: “They put us in some tough situations.” pic.twitter.com/N0leavIpFy — Nathan Canilao (@nathancanilao) November 7, 2026 “Experience is your best teacher,” Candle said. “The truth of the matter is, we've won football games, and he leaves the field with the same thought process that he wants some of those plays back. It’s just everybody else feels different around him. So, it's part of being the quarterback. He's a big boy. He understands what it is.” UNC jumped on Osborne early. On the Huskies ’ third possession of the game, Osborne’s pass was tipped at the line of scrimmage and was picked off by Timir Hickman-Collins, who returned the interception 62 yards for a touchdown. Later in the half, Osborne committed his second turnover. On a designed QB run, he attempted to reach for extra yardage by pushing the ball out in front of him. Unluckily for him, the ball fell right into the belly of Hickman-Collins. top.description: CHESTNUT HILL, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 07: Carter Jula #87 of the Florida State Seminoles tosses the football for a trick play in the first half against Boston College Eagles at Alumni Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) Getty The Florida State Seminoles pulled off one of the boldest plays of Saturday’s college football action against Boston College. With less than a minute remaining in the first half on Nov. 7, Florida State faced fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line. A short field goal appeared likely. Instead, kicker Gabe Panikowski took off running on a fake field goal attempt and crossed the goal line for a touchdown. The stunning play gave Florida State a 21-17 lead heading into halftime at Alumni Stadium. It also marked a memorable moment in Rick Stockstill’s first game as interim head coach. Florida State Kicker Gabe Panikowski Scores on Stunning Fake Field Goal Florida State trailed 17-14 late in the second quarter when quarterback Ashton Daniels led the Seminoles deep into Boston College territory. The offense stalled near the goal line, leaving Florida State with a decision on fourth down. The Seminoles lined up for a short field goal but had something else planned. Panikowski took the ball and raced toward the end zone, beating Boston College’s defense for a 1-yard rushing touchdown . The kicker then returned to his usual duties and converted the extra point. The sequence capped a 12-play, 63-yard drive that lasted 3:49. Florida State scored with 51 seconds left in the half. TJ Salomone shared footage of the play on X. Unbelievable call here. Florida State kicker Gabe Panikowski runs it in for the TD on the fake. 😱 pic.twitter.com/8m9RDeSOfe — TJ Salomone (@TJSalomone) November 7, 2026 “Unbelievable call here,” Salomone wrote. Panikowski entered Saturday with an impressive kicking streak of his own. According to Florida State’s official athletics website , he had made 23 consecutive field goals dating back to 2023. This time, his legs delivered six points rather than three. Florida State’s Bold Call Comes in Rick Stockstill’s First Game The fake arrived during a difficult stretch for Florida State’s football program. The Seminoles entered Saturday at 3-5 following three consecutive losses. Their latest setback, a 36-24 defeat against Clemson on Oct. 31, led to a coaching change. Florida State fired Mike Norvell on Nov. 1 and named Stockstill interim head coach. The former Middle Tennessee State coach inherited a team searching for its first road victory of the season. Boston College initially controlled Saturday’s matchup, building a 10-0 first-quarter lead. Daniels responded with a 4-yard rushing touchdown early in the second quarter. top.title: Hamilton & Verstappen to start from back in Brazil
top.description: Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will both start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix [Reuters] Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc and Mercedes' George Russell will also have grid penalties, 10 places for Leclerc and five for Russell. Russell qualified on the front row in second place on Saturday but will now drop down to seventh on the starting grid. Leclerc was fourth but will line up in 14th. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and the Audi of Nico Hulkenberg were fifth and sixth in the top-10 shootout, and with Russell and Leclerc's penalties applied, the two drivers have been lifted up on to the second row, in third and fourth respectively. Norris takes pole in rain-delayed qualifying Hamilton initially had only a 10-place penalty for exceeding his power-unit allowance for the season, but the new internal combustion engine that was fitted on Saturday morning failed in final practice. That meant Ferrari decided to fit an entire new power-unit to his car, hence the bigger penalty. Verstappen had an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice. Leclerc and Russell have both fitted new internal combustion engines. The penalty for Leclerc is bigger than Russell's because it is the first time Ferrari have exceeded the limit of four engines per season on his car, while Russell had already gone beyond that. The four drivers are separated by just 16 points in the drivers' championship, in the battle to finish second behind Kimi Antonelli. Verstappen famously won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race. Qualifying was wet, after rain started about an hour before the session, and it is expected to continue overnight, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day. Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035. F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo. "The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil." top.title: Rodrigo Mora: ‘Football is crazy sometimes, Cristiano Ronaldo my idol’
top.description: Rodrigo Mora: ‘Football is crazy sometimes, Cristiano Ronaldo my idol’ Rodrigo Mora concedes ‘football is crazy’ after scoring his third consecutive Serie A goal for Roma and looks forward to a senior Portugal debut even without ‘idol’ Cristiano Ronaldo. The 19-year-old talent was a big investment this summer from FC Porto, secured for €25m for effectively only half his contract. It took a while for him to make his mark in the Giallorossi jersey, but this evening he scored in the 3-0 win over Sassuolo , his third consecutive Serie A match on target. Rodrigo Mora happy at Roma ROME, ITALY – NOVEMBER 07: Rodrigo Mora of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s third goal with teammate Mario Hermoso during the Serie A match between AS Roma and US Sassuolo at Stadio Olimpico on November 07, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) “It was a very good pass from Malen, I tried my luck, and I was happy to score another important goal, so Roma keep pushing with another win,” Mora told Sky Sport Italia. He now has four goals in nine Serie A games, plus two assists in four Champions League appearances under Gian Piero Gasperini. “When I arrived here, I thought we were strong. Every time I training I thought we were a very good team, we are proving that in the match and need to keep this momentum going.” ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: Rodrigo Mora of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between AS Roma and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on October 27, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Mora seems to have really hit his stride in the last month, as after struggling to even get into the starting XI, he has flourished in recent weeks. “Football is crazy, because one day you don’t play, the next you play. I was ready, now it’s my third goal in a row, so it’s important to always be ready when the moment comes.” ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 14: Rodrigo Mora of AS Roma shoots under pressure from Antonio Rudiger of Real Madrid during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AS Roma and Real Madrid C.F. at Stadio Olimpico on October 14, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) Rodrigo Mora has also received a call-up for the senior Portugal squad, which will be a very different team now that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international duty. “It’s a very proud moment for me and my family, it is always a pleasure to play for Portugal. Now Cristiano is not there, but is an idol for everyone in Portugal, including me. I learned a lot when I came to the national team, I am very happy to be there.”

nigeria.title: Gas transportation network not responsible for power generation drop – NNPC
nigeria.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has said its gas transportation network remains available to supply gas to power generating stations nationwide, insisting that transportation constraints are not responsible for the current decline in electricity generation. The national oil company said operational records of its subsidiary, NNPC Gas Infrastructure Company Limited (NGIC), showed no transportation-related constraints within its network that could explain the drop in power generation. NNPC disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, in Abuja on Friday. The clarification followed a November 5 statement by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which attributed the decline in electricity generation partly to limited gas availability and reduced water inflows into hydroelectric power stations. However, NNPC said its clarification was specifically about the operational status of its gas transportation infrastructure, noting that gas production, commercial supply arrangements and actual deliveries to individual power plants were separate issues requiring independent assessment. The company said gas production had grown by about 10 per cent year-to-date in 2026, attributing the increase to the Federal Government’s gas development and monetisation agenda. “Gas supply availability is therefore not a challenge as NNPC remains committed to supporting efforts to improve electricity generation through safe, reliable and efficient gas supply and transportation,” the statement said. NNPC further explained that determining the causes of the generation shortfall required an assessment of other components of the gas-to-power value chain. These, it said, included the availability and operational readiness of generating units, plant maintenance schedules and actual gas offtake by power stations. The company stressed that the factors must be examined alongside gas supply data to establish the specific causes of the decline in electricity generation. It also called for a coordinated review of operational data by gas suppliers, transporters, power generators and NISO to identify constraints and guide appropriate interventions. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to developing dependable energy infrastructure and collaborating with stakeholders to translate the country’s gas resources into more reliable electricity supply for Nigerians. nigeria.title: Olawepo-Hashim visits Sowore, condemns political violence
nigeria.description: Former presidential candidate, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has condemned political violence in Nigeria, warning that attacks on political opponents could worsen the country’s already precarious security situation. Olawepo-Hashim also called on President Bola Tinubu to caution members of his team against actions and statements capable of provoking political conflict. He made the remarks in a statement posted on his X platform on Saturday after visiting activist and publisher, Omoyele Sowore, following the reported attack on him in Ekiti State. Olawepo-Hashim said his visit was motivated by their longstanding relationship, which dates back to their participation in the struggle against military dictatorship and the campaign for democracy. He warned that Nigeria, already grappling with terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security challenges, could not afford another crisis arising from political violence. “Nigeria cannot afford to add political violence to the general insecurity in the land. “Nigeria is already battling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and widespread insecurity. We cannot afford to add political violence to this burden,” he said. The former presidential candidate welcomed a statement by a United Nations representative expressing concern over the incident and urged other international partners to condemn political violence. He also urged political leaders to exercise restraint, warning that those who provoke violence might not be the ones to suffer its consequences. “President Bola Tinubu must call his team to order. Political leaders must exercise restraint and stop actions or rhetoric capable of provoking conflict. Those who recklessly provoke violence may not be the ones who bear its consequences,” he said. Recalling their history, Olawepo-Hashim said he and Sowore had been comrades since 1989/1990, when they worked together against military rule. He said he was particularly moved by Sowore’s recollection of how he introduced him to political activism at the University of Lagos. According to him, Sowore reaffirmed during the visit that he remained undeterred by the reported attack and was determined to continue campaigning for genuine democracy. Olawepo-Hashim stressed that political disagreements should not be used as justification for violence, urging Nigerians to uphold democratic values and reject actions capable of worsening insecurity and instability in the country. nigeria.title: Trump orders Justice Department probe of Democrats seeking impeachment
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration. Trump faces a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterms. Democrats have vowed investigations into Trump and senior members of his administration, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. “The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. “This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable,” he said, arguing that there had been “no impeachable acts committed.” Trump said he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act” and said “imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS.” With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny. Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. “Lawyer up,” wrote incoming House Oversight Committee chairman Robert Garcia on X as the results became clear on election night. Democrats have also signaled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles. Democrats could pursue Trump’s third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so. The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate — far beyond the party’s numbers. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win first U-17 Women’s World Cup
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, have defeated Japan 2-1 to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Flamingos secured the historic victory on Saturday at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat, to claim their first title in the competition. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring for Nigeria in the 39th minute with a long-range effort that slipped through the hands of the Japanese goalkeeper. Nigeria doubled their advantage shortly after the restart, with Oluebube Umejiaku finding the net in the 47th minute to put the Flamingos in control. Japan fought back and reduced the deficit through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute. The Japanese side pushed for an equaliser, but Nigeria held on to secure the 2-1 victory. The Flamingos also came close to extending their lead late in the game, striking the crossbar from a corner kick. Road to victory Flamingos’ campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. nigeria.title: EPL: Delap double condemns Man City to third straight defeat
nigeria.description: Manchester City slumped to a third consecutive Premier League defeat on Saturday as Liam Delap’s double lifted Nottingham Forest out of the relegation zone with a 3-1 win at the City Ground. Oliver Glasner’s men had not scored at home at all this season, but pounced on City’s defensive errors to strike twice in the first 20 minutes through Jair Cunha and Delap. Rayan Cherki’s stunning strike gave City hope, but their title challenge is rapidly wilting even before the potential effects of a major points deduction. Delap sealed just Forest’s second win of the season with an incredible strike in off the post on the night that could launch his career for the two-time European champions, after a difficult start since his club-record £50 million ($67 million) move from Chelsea. Defeat leaves City six points adrift of leaders Arsenal and with questions over whether the uncertainty surrounding the club is playing a part in their on-field slump. Found guilty on over 100 Premier League charges of breaking financial rules, the 10-time English champions face a severe points penalty unless they can overturn that verdict on appeal. Glasner warned his players he would make big changes after a disappointing start to his reign saw them start the match in the bottom three. The Austrian got the response he craved as Forest burst out of the blocks to pounce on City’s sloppiness at the back. – Clinical Forest – Cunha robbed Josko Gvardiol midway inside the City half and was allowed to bear down on goal before slotting past Gianluigi Donnarumma. nigeria.title: Rivers crisis: You’ll not regret choosing peace, Tinubu assures Fubara
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has assured Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, that he would not regret his decision to embrace peace and respect the intervention of political elders in resolving the crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu gave the assurance on Saturday while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt. He said, “To me, I intervened on your behalf. Similarly, to Fubara, Your Excellency, the host governor of today, I want to thank you specifically for maturity, understanding, respect for the wisdom of elders. “When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat, Fubara. You will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” Tinubu said. The political crisis, which erupted in October 2023, followed a breakdown in relations between Fubara and his predecessor, now Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, over control of the state’s political structure. The crisis escalated in March 2025 when Tinubu declared a state of emergency in the state , suspending Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and members of the House of Assembly for six months. Fubara returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule. However, political tensions resurfaced, with lawmakers initiating another impeachment process against him and his deputy in January 2026. Efforts to reconcile the feuding camps gained momentum in June 2025 when Tinubu convened a meeting involving Fubara, Wike and members of the Rivers State House of Assembly at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. More recently, in October , Fubara and Wike held another reconciliation meeting in Port Harcourt alongside their supporters, in what was seen as an effort to consolidate the rapprochement between the two political camps. nigeria.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
nigeria.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games. Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat. Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range. – VAR controversy – In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw. nigeria.title: Tinubu to Nigerian youths: Your future depends on 2027 election
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerian youths to collect their Permanent Voter Cards and participate actively in the 2027 general elections, saying the outcome of the poll will have a direct bearing on their future. Tinubu made the call on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Addressing the youths at the rally, the president said the election should not be viewed as being about his personal ambition but about determining the future of the younger generation. “To the youth of Nigeria, I’m looking at you. This election is about you. It’s not about me. Your future depends on this election,” he said. Tinubu urged Nigerians who were yet to collect their PVCs to do so, describing the voter card as the means through which citizens could determine the country’s leadership. “It is left for you to use the weapon you have. And that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it. Please. I beg you. “I take God, beg you,” he said. The president also identified economic development as a key tool for young Nigerians to overcome poverty, saying his administration was working to improve the economy and ensure that prosperity was widely shared. He said previous administrations had left behind unpaid pensions and gratuities running into billions and trillions of naira, adding that his government was clearing the outstanding obligations. “The people that governed before left unpaid pensions and gratuity in billions and trillions of naira. That is being cleared. So that every family is included. We are sharing prosperity already,” Tinubu said. He listed retired professionals, including engineers, welders, and teachers, among those benefiting from the payments. “A retired engineer is receiving their gratuity right now. A retired welder is receiving the pension right now. A retired teacher is receiving the pension right now,” he added. business.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. SHOW AND AVAILABILITY Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. sports.description: Just as they have done all year, the Notre Dame Pandas volleyball team overcame a bit of adversity to take down Whitley County 26-24, 19-25, 25-14, 25-14 in the 2026 Kentucky High School Athletic Association state semifinals. "It's a hard match when you don't have any history with another team. We just knew that they were going to come out and give it everything that they've got. We just couldn't let up. We had to figure out a few things and make a few adjustments," Notre Dame co-coach Hannah Colvin said. Even though they played in the second semifinal of the day, the Pandas came out a little sluggish, allowing the Colonels to surge to a 16-13 lead in the first set. But five straight points, highlighted by two Teagan Kondik aces, gave them an 18-16 lead. Behind 13th Region Player of the Year Regan Isaac, Whitley County took a set point at 24-23 before kills from Ellie Breitling and Kondik gave the Pandas a 1-0 advantage. Isaac, Shelbi Carroll and Jada Smith continued to wreak havoc on the Pandas' defense in the second set, combining for 16 kills, Regan responsible for 12 on her own. Despite hitting .220, the Colonels benefitted from six Panda attack errors. "(Isaac) was really good. Our game plan was to keep it away from her and get in her head to make mistakes. That second set, we were making more mistakes than they were," Notre Dame senior Ellie Osterkamp said. In the third set, NDA played a deeper back row to take away Isaac's preferred corner attack angle. While that put more responsibility on the block, NDA came up with two rejections and forced Whitley County into seven more attack errors. The Pandas grabbed a 4-0 lead, then surged to a 11-5 advantage after five straight Colonel errors. Dara Jackson finished off the set with the first of her two aces. sports.title: Could Gina Hinojosa reshape Texas Tech's board and put Cody Campbell's chairmanship at risk?
sports.description: Texas Tech regent Cody Campbell and Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark clash over a potential Friday night game, escalating tensions over scheduling and control. (LM Otero/Associated Press) Texas' blue wave could cost one of college sports' most powerful billionaires a seat on the Texas Tech University System Board of Regents and put his chairmanship at risk. Cody Campbell, a former Texas Tech offensive lineman and oilman, has wielded significant influence over the Red Raiders since Gov. Greg Abbott appointed him to the board in 2021. Campbell's six-year term expires Jan. 31, shortly after Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa takes office. The governor appoints regents, who must be confirmed by the state Senate. The Texas Tech board elects its chair from among its members, so Hinojosa's appointments could affect who leads it. The Senate remains under Republican control and could serve as a check on her choices. As chairman, Campbell has become an influential figure in Texas Tech athletics and the broader debate over the future of college sports. He also took a public role in the program's response to quarterback Brendan Sorsby's legal battle over his sports betting history. Campbell, co-founder and co-CEO of Double Eagle Energy Holdings, became a billionaire through the oil and gas industry. He is a close ally and adviser to President Donald Trump on college sports, serving on both Trump's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition and his college sports council. He was also among the earliest members of the America First Policy Institute, a conservative think tank associated with the Trump administration, and has been a major donor to Republican candidates. Even if Campbell loses his board seat, he could retain significant financial influence over Red Raiders athletics. He and business partner John Sellers founded the Red Raiders' NIL collective, which supports player recruitment and roster retention. sports.title: 3 keys to victory for the Broncos against the Panthers
sports.description: After the difficult schedule the Denver Broncos have faced through eight weeks of the 2026 season, the Carolina Panthers likely look like a welcome relief for most. However, in the NFL, there is rarely such a thing as an "easy win." The Panthers will have had nine days to prepare for a home game against the Broncos . They will also have the advantage that the East Coast team has when a team from the West Coast makes the long trip for an early kickoff. Head coach Sean Payton will have his team ready to keep its momentum rolling, looking for a fifth straight win, but the Broncos will need to follow these three keys to get that win and avoid a big letdown on the road. Broncos' keys to victory over Panthers in Week 9 Get after Bryce Young The Panthers are going to try to establish their rushing attack, led by Chuba Hubbard, to attempt to negate the Broncos' pass rush. The Panthers have allowed 23 sacks this season, the second-most in the league, and their offensive line is missing starting right tackle Taylor Moton, who is out for the season. The Broncos need to come after Bryce Young on every passing down in this game. As strong as the secondary is, Vance Joseph can trust it to hold up in this one and dial up frequent blitzes to have Young scrambling just to get the ball out of his hands on nearly every dropback. This is the kind of game where the Broncos not only could have a bunch of sacks; they should. Expose Carolina's run defense The Broncos have struggled to move the ball on the ground this season, averaging only 92.6 rushing yards per game, 26th in the league. But the Panthers rank 30th in defending the run, giving up almost 141 yards per game. This is the game for the Broncos to get that running game going. Jonah Coleman had a solid performance last week against the Kansas City Chiefs, and if he can follow that up with another big game here, the momentum from that could carry into the latter stages of the season. If the Broncos can establish the run in this game and rip off six- or seven-yard chunks at a time, it will open things up for the offense and make the third key to victory that much easier to accomplish. Be aggressive with Bo Nix While the Panthers have struggled to defend against the run, they have been much more difficult to throw against, ranking 10th in the league in that category. Still, the defense as a whole has not been good. The Panthers gave up 59 points to the Chicago Bears in a game this season and that was at home. Payton needs to be aggressive with his play-calling and allow Bo Nix to open things up in the passing game. Nix should attempt to throw the ball deep down the field in this one, especially if the Broncos can get the run game going and he can use the play-action to his advantage. No disrespect to Carolina as an opponent, but the Broncos should use this game to boost the level the offense is currently playing at and see if they can develop some trends to carry through the rest of the season. sports.title: Wolff delivers verdict on costly Mercedes call that left Russell furious
sports.description: Toto Wolff has defended Mercedes' decision to instruct George Russell to back off during his final qualifying attempt at the Brazilian Grand Prix , describing it as a 50-50 call despite admitting the Briton deserved pole position. Russell was left furious during the closing stages of Q3 at Interlagos after being told to abandon a promising lap when he encountered Alex Albon's Williams ahead of him. The Mercedes driver was already second behind Lando Norris and appeared capable of challenging for pole, having set purple times in the first two sectors. However, his race engineer instructed him to slow down, with the team expecting another opportunity before the rain intensified. That opportunity never came, prompting an angry reaction from Russell over team radio , with Wolff himself intervening to remind the driver that he was still second. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Wolff reveals how close Russell was to Norris Speaking to Sky Sports F1 after qualifying, Wolff acknowledged the difficulty of making the right decision as the weather deteriorated: "If we were to have a crystal ball to know whether you should back off or not, that would be helpful It was a difficult one, a 50-50 call. He was running into Albon." Wolff also revealed how close Russell was to Norris at the moment the instruction was given, although he questioned whether the Briton would ultimately have completed a lap fast enough to take pole. "He was 18 milliseconds up on Norris at that stage. I don't think it would have been enough for pole, but he drove perfectly all session and merited to be on pole." Despite his doubts about whether Russell could have beaten Norris' benchmark, Wolff praised the Mercedes driver's performance throughout the rain-affected session: "He deserved it but you can't make that call. It's 50 per cent right or wrong. George was in a league of his own today." Russell ultimately finished qualifying second, 0.204 seconds behind Norris, but will start Sunday's race from seventh following a five-place grid penalty for a power unit change. His teammate Kimi Antonelli, who qualified third, will instead line up alongside Norris on the front row.

sports.title: Michael Carrick backs Bruno Fernandes and insists attitude is ‘as good as ever’
sports.description: Michael Carrick said Bruno Fernandes ’ attitude is “as good as ever” and he has no doubts about his commitment again after their falling-out. The United manager dropped his captain after Fernandes criticised his tactics during the 4-1 defeat to Como and chose not to bring him on in the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth. But Carrick and Fernandes held talks last week and the Portuguese returned to the team at Chelsea on Saturday before playing his part in their comeback win over Roma, scoring their first goal with a twice-taken penalty and providing the assist for Matheus Cunha’s equaliser. “I think by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and frame of mind he was in for that, I think that tells everything,” said Carrick. “Yeah, Bruno's as good as ever.” The 45-year-old has not revealed if Fernandes apologised to him, adding: “What's actually said in that discussion, you'll be pleased to know I'll keep that to myself. “But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me of what he brings to this team and this club, and I think he showed that again this week.” Carrick has challenged Cunha to replicate his catalytic display against Roma, when he won a penalty and scored two goals, to double his tally for the season. “He has to repeat that performance,” the United manager said. “He was fantastic and that's close to his best, and that's the level where we want to see.” Carrick has said before that he has not sought reassurances about his position during United’s slump and they have only won one of their last 10 games in all competitions. He has not been told he will remain in charge next week. “No, no,” he replied, adding that his plans were unchanged. “Just carry on as absolute normal.”

sports.title: Hamilton & Verstappen to start from back in Brazil
sports.description: Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will both start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix [Reuters] Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc and Mercedes' George Russell will also have grid penalties, 10 places for Leclerc and five for Russell. Russell qualified on the front row in second place on Saturday but will now drop down to seventh on the starting grid. Leclerc was fourth but will line up in 14th. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and the Audi of Nico Hulkenberg were fifth and sixth in the top-10 shootout, and with Russell and Leclerc's penalties applied, the two drivers have been lifted up on to the second row, in third and fourth respectively. Norris takes pole in rain-delayed qualifying Hamilton initially had only a 10-place penalty for exceeding his power-unit allowance for the season, but the new internal combustion engine that was fitted on Saturday morning failed in final practice. That meant Ferrari decided to fit an entire new power-unit to his car, hence the bigger penalty. Verstappen had an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice. Leclerc and Russell have both fitted new internal combustion engines. The penalty for Leclerc is bigger than Russell's because it is the first time Ferrari have exceeded the limit of four engines per season on his car, while Russell had already gone beyond that. The four drivers are separated by just 16 points in the drivers' championship, in the battle to finish second behind Kimi Antonelli. Verstappen famously won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race. Qualifying was wet, after rain started about an hour before the session, and it is expected to continue overnight, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day. Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035. F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo. "The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil." science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments."
